newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Philippines bonds on review, may upgrade-Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Philippines bonds on review, may upgrade-Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday it has placed Philippines' foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds and notes on review for possible upgrade from the current Ba2 rating.
Moody's said the review was prompted by the successful macro-economic policies implemented by the government in recent years, in particular the substantial effort made in fiscal adjustment.

The government's commitment to strengthening its fiscal accounts has been reflected in its pursuit and implementation of important tax measures, including an expanded value-added-tax and the crucial excise tax passed last November, it said.
This will bolster its revenue base and reduce its dependence on one-off privatisation receipts, the rating agency said.
Structural reforms have improved the economy's international competitiveness, encouarged increased foreign investor interest, reduce inflation and triggered a robust export performance, Moody's said.
The external foreign currency debt burden has moderated, it said.
As part of the review process, Moody's said it will focus both the political and economic factors affecting the sustainability of these favourable developments over the medium-term.
